qs.q: A Level 2 home charger runs on:
qs.why: Level 1 uses a regular 120 V outlet. Level 2 uses the kind of circuit a dryer uses.

qs.q: How does Level 2 charging compare with Level 1?
qs.why: Level 1 adds only a few kilometres of range per hour. Level 2 can refill most cars overnight.

qs.q: Before installing a charger, what does an electrician check?
qs.why: A load calculation shows if your panel has room or needs a smart device or an upgrade.

qs.q: Which is a common way to connect a Level 2 charger?
qs.why: Hardwiring is simple and often preferred for outdoor use.

options: Schedules charging for cheap overnight rates
qs.why: Many chargers and cars let you set a start time.

qs.q: A 7 kW charger delivers about how much energy in an hour?
qs.why: A kilowatt is power. Multiply by hours to get kilowatt-hours.

qs.q: What does a load management device do?
options: Shares panel capacity so the charger does not overload it
qs.why: It can avoid an expensive panel upgrade.

qs.q: What should an outdoor charger be?
qs.why: Look for an enclosure rating that suits rain, snow and sun.

options: Different cars use different plugs, and adapters exist
qs.why: The plug on your car and the one on the charger must match, or you need an adapter.

qs.q: Charging at home on a normal rate usually costs:
qs.why: Electricity is generally cheaper than fuel for the same distance, and off-peak rates can cut it more.
